paragraphs.zh: Tabelle 3:  Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen der allgemeinen Formel (I), worin die Substituenten und Symbole folgende Bedeutungen haben:
paragraphs.en: Table 3:  Compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I), in which the substituents and symbols have the following meanings:
paragraphs.notes: The only German prose on the page. Printed over two lines with 'Tabelle 3:' in bold and the rest in the regular face; the second line is indented to align under 'Erfindungsgemäße'. Umlaut and eszett are as printed (Erfindungsgemäße). The caption states that the table enumerates compounds of the invention, not prior art. A small ink speck sits directly above the 'a' of 'haben' at the end of the second line; it is a scan artifact, not a diacritic, and is not transcribed.

paragraphs.zh: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Et R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.en: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Et R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.notes: The block of fixed substituent values printed under the caption, laid out as three rows of three definitions across the page. The superscript locants on R2, R3, R4, R5 and R6 are printed as true superscripts and the digits of SO2Et and CH2 as true subscripts; both are flattened to plain text here, and the wide column gaps are approximated with spaces. These cells are chemical symbols and single letters, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string. Note that R1 and L are NOT fixed here: they are the two columns the table below varies.

Markush enumeration table, compound numbers 390 to 400, with a shaded header row. The cells are chemical symbols and NMR data, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string; the only German in the grid is the header cell 'Physikalische Daten' ('Physical data'), left as printed. Typography as printed: the header cell R1 carries a superscript 1; the digits in CH2, OCH2CHF2, OCH2CF3, OCH2CH2Cl, SCH2CF3, OCH2CH2Br, OCH2CH2F, OCH2CF2CF2H, OCH2CF2CF3, OCH2CF2CF2CF3, CH2CH2 and CDCl3 are subscripts, and the leading '1' of '1H NMR' is a superscript; all are rendered inline here. The chemical shift symbol at the head of each data cell is a lower case Greek delta, written 'd' here to keep the transcription ASCII, followed by a wide gap before the first shift, which is preserved. Rows 394 to 400 have an empty Physikalische Daten cell as printed; the trailing ' | ' with nothing after it records that. Transcribed as printed without correction: row 390 lists 3.98 (q,2H) before 3.95 (m,2H), so the shifts are not in ascending order; row 392 lists 7.32 (d,2H) where the other four data rows give (d,1H) at the corresponding aromatic position; rows 392 and 393 contain a double space, and rows 391 and 393 print 'q, 2H' with a space after the comma while the rest print 'q,2H'. A short stray tick sits just to the right of the '394' in the Nr. column; it is a scan artifact, not a character.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st and only, centred between the fixed substituent block and the table header row; the generic scaffold that Tabelle 3 enumerates
structures.core: two rings joined by a ketone bridge: a cyclohex-2-ene-1,3-dione drawn in its enol form (3-hydroxycyclohex-2-en-1-one) on the left, and a benzene ring drawn with three inner double bonds on the right
substituents: on the cyclohexenone ring: OH at C3, drawn as a label above the ring vertex that carries the ring double bond
on the cyclohexenone ring: =O at C1, drawn as a doubly bonded O to the lower right of the ring
on the cyclohexenone ring: the aroyl bridge at C2, the vertex between the OH-bearing and the =O-bearing carbons, which carries the ring double bond to C3
on the cyclohexenone ring: three unlabelled CH2 vertices at C4, C5 and C6
bridge: C=O, drawn as a vertex with a doubly bonded O above it, joining C2 of the cyclohexenone to C1 of the benzene ring
on the benzene ring: the C=O bridge at C1 (the upper left vertex)
on the benzene ring: Cl at C2 (the top vertex)
on the benzene ring: L-R1 at C3, drawn as a bond from the ring to the label L and a further horizontal bond from L to the label R with superscript 1
on the benzene ring: SO2Et at C4, drawn as a bond from the ring to S, with two doubly bonded O below the S and the label Et to its upper right
on the benzene ring: H at C5 (a plain unlabelled ring vertex)
on the benzene ring: H at C6 (a plain unlabelled ring vertex)

drawings.notes: The locants above are a reading convention for this record and are not printed on the drawing. On the benzene ring C1 is the carbon bearing the ketone bridge and the numbering runs towards the chlorine, which sits on the adjacent carbon as drawn; the bridge, Cl, L-R1 and SO2Et occupy four consecutive ring carbons in that order and the two remaining vertices, on the lower left edge, are unlabelled. On the cyclohexenone ring C1 is the ketone carbon and C3 the enol carbon bearing OH, with the aroyl bridge on C2 between them and the drawn double bond between C2 and C3. Every position is read off the drawing only; the scan is clean and no position is ambiguous. name and smiles are null because L and R1 are undefined variables on this drawing: writing either would mean choosing values the drawing does not fix. presented_as is intermediate_structure in the sense this run uses for a generic Markush scaffold that a table enumerates; the caption above it says plainly that these are erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen (compounds according to the invention) of the general formula (I), so this is the invention's own subject matter and NOT prior art. There is no reaction scheme on this page and no arrow of any kind.

discrepancies.what: The fixed substituent block defines nine symbols, but only R2, R3 and R6 can be matched to a label or a drawn group on the scaffold; R4, R5, Y, Z, v and w appear nowhere on the drawing.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The benzene ring carries Cl and SO2Et as drawn text, the cyclohexenone carries a drawn OH, and the remaining ring vertices are plain unlabelled vertices with no R4, R5, Y, Z, v or w label anywhere on the page.
discrepancies.text_says: R2 = Cl, R3 = SO2Et, R4 = H, R5 = H, R6 = OH, Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1, w = 0.

discrepancies.what: Row 392 gives a two proton integral for an aromatic doublet where the other four data rows give a one proton doublet at the same position.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The scaffold has exactly two unlabelled benzene CH vertices, so the aromatic region can carry at most two aromatic protons in total, which rows 390, 391 and 393 report as two separate one proton doublets.
